This Washington runner had her race stolen by a trans-identified male. Now she’s speaking out.

Lily Bennett ran the fastest race of her life. It should have earned her a spot on the state podium.

Instead, she went home without a medal.

After years of training and overcoming a stress fracture, Lily finished 17th at Washington’s state cross-country championship, just ONE spot shy of the podium.

Then she learned why.

A male had placed 13th in her race. According to Lily, that same athlete’s time would have placed 153rd out of 160 competitors in the boys’ race.

But it’s about more than a medal. It’s about college recruitment, scholarship opportunities, and years of hard work.

“Every place matters. Every place has meaning,” Lily told IW Features.

Now, Lily is speaking out. And earlier this month, Washington voters passed Initiative 638, restoring sex-based athletic competition beginning December 3.

It’s a victory for future female athletes, but it cannot give Lily back the moment she earned.

Girls deserve a fair playing field. Period.

posts.text:
I'm hearing several rumors that frontier labs have broken some major cryptographic primitives:

- "Factoring is in P": Now that the Riemann hypothesis is proven, we do understand much better how primes are distributed. Still, I don't think factoring is in P. 
AKS showed in 2002 that primality testing (deciding whether a number is prime) is in P, but factoring is a different beast. If it were in P, RSA would simply be broken, and that would be huge: a large part of our systems still rely on RSA.

- "ECC has been broken": Other rumors say elliptic-curve cryptography has been cryptanalyzed, which would take down ECDH and ECDSA along with it. (all the non-RSA asymmetric cryptography)

- Ring-LWE isn't quantum-resistant. That wouldn't be an immediate threat, since there's no cryptographically relevant quantum computer yet. But it would make the ongoing post-quantum migration pointless.

It's hard to tell what's true. AI has made incredible progress, starting with the proof of the Riemann hypothesis. 

And most importantly, if a frontier lab did find something like this, a clean responsible disclosure that avoids mass exploitation would be very hard to pull off. All of this helps the rumors spread.

Personally, I don't think findings like these are coming. I wouldn't be surprised if some of these primitives turn out to be a bit weaker than we thought, but I'd be very surprised to see any of them fall apart completely.
